justification: Version 3 changes one rule of version 2 (budget-policy.v2.json, SHA-256 f9eab3d12f0f110e888c5f40bfc752674d2ff2245e046de92574123ca8d1fd12): the two synthetic-c10000-t1000-r100-s307 peak-RSS budgets (full.maxRssBytes and session.maxRssBytes) are judged on the minimum over all samples instead of the median, with an absolute limit of the baseline minimum times the memory-rule factor. Cause, a calibration defect of version 2: peak RSS of these cells is bimodal on the measurement host too. Diagnosed on the CE-01.1 candidate (35a6629) and alpha1 in an admissible run: when a V8 mark-compact lands around 19 s, mid full compile, with about 520 MB live, the next heap limit is about 4x that and the session peaks at 2.1-2.2 GB; otherwise it stays near 1.2-1.4 GB. alpha1 itself reaches the high mode in about 25% of rounds (4 of 22 pooled), so it would fail its own version 2 limit about 10% of the time. Every version 2 baseline sample happened to be in the low mode, so version 2 measured a CV of 0.5% and derived an absolute median limit. Garbage-collector headroom is one-sided additive noise on peak RSS, so the minimum estimates the working-set floor and absorbs high-mode rounds, which stay in the evidence. Real growth of the floor is still caught: in the same diagnosis the candidate low-mode growth was +9.2% (ratio 1.092, interval 1.074 to 1.116), from about 25 MB of additional live data amplified about 4x by V8, and with --max-old-space-size=1536 both epochs stay below 1 GB. The limit factor follows the unchanged memory rule (floor 1.10, 1 + 3 CV) applied to the CV of the minima of each baseline run and epoch. The statistic is an explicit per-budget field (thresholdRule.statistic): median by default; min allowed only for absolute peak-RSS memory budgets, refused anywhere else, and unknown statistics are refused. Every other rule is unchanged: the 1.25 timing floor, runtime and memory floors, the memory rule, deterministic growth, identity, metrics, workloads, noise ceiling, minimum pairs and rounding. As the change policy requires, every budget is re-derived from a new comparable baseline of the unchanged alpha1 artifact, measured on the same measurement host as version 2 (alpha1-v3-sk-c1 and alpha1-v3-sk-c4, the first two admissible attempts of the pre-registered series C); the version 2 evidence is not reused. Every budget whose derived limit loosens relative to version 2 is listed in relaxations, generated from the derivation. The absolute limits remain bound to the measurement host. Recovery of the CE-01.1 cost remains owned by CE-12.3 (#76).

comparison: Run tools/baselines/measure.mjs with the final plan and both --epoch alpha1=<alpha1 closure> and --epoch <candidate>=<candidate closure> on one machine (--require-quiet is optional). budgets.mjs gate pairs each candidate sample with the adjacent alpha1 sample of the same round, applies the paired-ratio, absolute-memory, deterministic and identity budgets, requires alpha1 to reproduce its frozen deterministic outputs, and lists unknown metrics. Verdicts: pass only when every budget passes; fail on any failing budget, workload-record mismatch, altered alpha1 tarball or policy-chain problem; inconclusive when the run lacks the interleaved control, has too few pairs, exceeds a noise ceiling or cannot resolve a limit; incomplete when a budgeted metric was not run.

changePolicy: budgets.v3.json is generated by `node tools/baselines/budgets.mjs freeze` from this policy and the committed baseline results, and is never edited by hand; rerunning the same freeze command with this policy and the referenced results must reproduce it byte for byte.

Committed policy, budgets, workloads, derivation and baseline result files are immutable; `budgets.mjs gate` compares the budgets file with the version of the commit that added it and fails on any difference.

Changing a threshold, metric set or workload requires a new budget-policy.vN.json and budgets.vN.json (N incremented), a justification, a predecessor reference by path and SHA-256, and a new comparable baseline run of the unchanged alpha1 artifact; reusing an old result file is rejected.
Every budget loosened or removed relative to the predecessor must be listed in `relaxations` with its own justification; an unknown metric may only leave the unknown list by gaining a budget.

No release may pass against a weakened budget retroactively: the gate evaluates the budgets version current at the evaluated commit, fails on any policy-chain problem, and never reports inconclusive or incomplete as pass.
